Priya Rao: Ran a mixed-precision routing sweep on staging (a8g-16 / gtx-pool). Saw a weird regression when INT8 kernels are enabled for attention middle blocks — tail latency up ~12% for 2048 context.
Tom F.: :eyes: did you pin the same kernel selection policy? sometimes the fallback chooses slower FP16 kernels if mismatch happens.
Priya Rao: I forced kernel selection with `--prefer-int8` in the runtime and still saw the spike. Attached microprofile below.
Maria L.: can you paste the perf counters and the kv-cache hit distribution? might be cache thrash when switching kernels mid-request.
Priya Rao: sure. kv-cache hits look stable (~98%). Here's the condensed profiler output (per-layer latency ms):
```
Layer  LayerType  QuantMode  Median(ms)  P99(ms)
0      Embedding  FP16       6.2         9.1
1      Attn1      INT8       3.4         7.8
2      MLP1       INT8       4.0         8.2
3      Attn2      FP8        3.8         6.9
4      MLP2       INT8       4.5         9.5  <-- sensitive
n-1    LM_head    FP16       2.1         3.0
```
Note: layers 2 and 4 spike on certain batches with long sequences.
Evan K.: Those 'sensitive' MLP layers might be tripping a different GEMM path (small m/k shapes). If the kernel auto-selector swaps to a non-optimized INT8 kernel, throughput drops.
Tom F.: plausible. Also batching heuristics: are we re-batching while kv-cache hits cause non-uniform seq lengths? that can create inconsistent shapes and kernel thrash.
Priya Rao: I reproduced with a synthetic workload: fixed prompt prefix then random tails. When I pin per-layer quant to INT8 except embeddings+lm_head (kept FP16), tail latency is back to baseline. Perf diff when switching per-layer quant at runtime shows a context switch cost.
Maria L.: do we have a cost model in the selector for quantized kernel warm-up penalty? if not, selector might prefer lower FLOPS kernels even if cold.
Priya Rao: not currently. Also noticed that calibration noise for FP8 during calibration pass can flip which kernel is selected — small calibration deltas change kernel scoring.
perfbot: [perf-regression] alert: staging/e2e-mixedprecision saw 11.7% increase in 99th latency vs baseline at 2026-03-15T14:12Z. CI run: https://ci.redwood/prof/1769553209 :warning:
Tom F.: next steps: 1) add a warm-up penalty in kernel selector for previously-unseen quant kernels; 2) expose per-layer overrides in rollout config; 3) run longer-tail synthetic tests with kv-cache enabled.
Evan K.: I'll prototype a selector heuristic: prefer kernels that match median sequence length and penalize switching mid-request. Will also add a fallback threshold for INT8 -> FP16 rather than sudden swap.
Priya Rao: I'll push a small telemetry change to emit kernel-selection events per-request so we can correlate with kv-cache and batch sizes. putting a canary on dedicated for 12hrs.
Maria L.: And let's add a quick eval: compare quality delta for partial-quant (exclude embeddings/lm_head/first-attn) vs full-quant on our calibration sets.
Tom F.: agreed. keep the canary narrow. If latency stabilizes, we can encode per-layer safe-list for quantization in our model metadata.
Priya Rao: thanks. tagging ops: @Evan K. @Tom F. will update thread when canary metrics land. :thumbsup:
